title: Matrix products and aligned printing
prompt:
Use these integer matrices, written row by row with the rows separated by `;`:
- A = `[2 -1 0; 1 3 -2; 0 4 1]` (3 rows, 3 columns)
- B = `[1 2; -3 0; 5 -1]` (3 rows, 2 columns)
- C = `[2 -1; 1 3]` (2 rows, 2 columns)
- D = `[3 1 2 -1; 1 2 0 -2; 4 -1 6 -3; 5 0 2 1]` (4 rows, 4 columns)
Print these five results in this order. Each matrix result is a title line followed by the rows of the matrix:
1. title `A*B`: the matrix product of A and B (A on the left).
2. title `(A*B)^T`: the transpose of that product (row i of the transpose is column i of the product).
3. title `C^6`: the product of six copies of C.
4. title `A*A-3A+2I`: the product of A with itself, minus 3 times A, plus 2 times the 3 by 3 identity matrix.
5. the determinant of D, printed as a single line `det(D) = N`, with no rows after it.
How to print the rows of a matrix: within that matrix, each column is as wide as its longest entry (a minus sign counts as a character); every entry is right-aligned to its column's width, and neighbouring columns are separated by two spaces. Widths are computed separately for each printed matrix. No line has trailing spaces.
